title: Sensitive Data Must Not Be Logged
description: Passwords, authentication tokens, API keys, session identifiers, credentials, and other secrets must not be written to application logs, console output, debug output, or error messages.
riskExplanation: Sensitive values in logs can be exposed through monitoring systems, support tools, error reporting, backups, or unauthorized log access.
suggestedAction: Remove the sensitive value from the log statement. If operational logging is necessary, log only a non-sensitive event, correlation ID, masked identifier, or user ID.
saferExample: logger.info('Login attempt received for user_id=%s', user_id)

supportingRegulatoryContext.title: Security of processing
supportingRegulatoryContext.relationship: Supporting security context only. This is not a legal-compliance conclusion.

title: Personal Data in Logs Must Be Minimized
description: Personal data should not be written to logs unless it is necessary for a defined operational purpose and adequately protected.
riskExplanation: Logs may be retained, exported, monitored, shared, or accessed by people who do not require the personal data for debugging or operations.
suggestedAction: Consider using a non-sensitive internal user ID, event ID, masked value, or correlation ID instead of logging the full personal-data value.
saferExample: logger.info('Profile update requested for user_id=%s', user_id)

supportingRegulatoryContext.title: Data minimisation
supportingRegulatoryContext.relationship: Potentially relevant where personal data is logged excessively or without a clear operational need. This is not a legal-compliance conclusion.

title: Silent Exception Handling Must Be Avoided
description: Empty exception handlers or bare exception passes suppress operational failures and impede security incident response.
riskExplanation: Silent failures hide security incidents, unauthorized access attempts, or system degradation from monitoring tools.
suggestedAction: Log exception context using logger.exception() or handle specific exceptions appropriately.

title: Hardcoded Secrets and API Tokens Must Be Avoided
description: Plaintext secret keys, passwords, API tokens, or JWT signing secrets hardcoded in source code risk exposure via version control.
riskExplanation: Hardcoded credentials in source control can be extracted by unauthorized users, external auditors, or automated repository scrapers.
suggestedAction: Load credentials dynamically from environment variables or a secure key management system.

title: Weak Cryptographic Hash Functions Must Not Be Used
description: Obsolete hash algorithms like MD5 or SHA-1 are vulnerable to collision attacks and must not be used for security purposes.
riskExplanation: Attackers can generate cryptographic hash collisions to forge digital signatures, tokens, or pass validation checks.
suggestedAction: Use strong cryptographic hash functions such as SHA-256 or secure password hashing algorithms like bcrypt or argon2.

supportingRegulatoryContext.title: Transitions: Recommendation for Transitioning the Use of Cryptographic Algorithms

title: SQL Queries Must Use Parameterized Input
description: Constructing SQL statements using string concatenation or f-strings creates critical SQL injection vulnerabilities.
riskExplanation: Unsanitized user input concatenated into SQL queries allows attackers to execute arbitrary database commands or exfiltrate data.
suggestedAction: Use parameterized queries or ORMs to pass user input separately from SQL command syntax.

title: Dynamic Shell Execution Must Be Avoided
description: Executing shell commands via os.system or subprocess with shell=True introduces command injection risks.
riskExplanation: Attackers supplying metacharacters (e.g. ';', '|', '`') in inputs can execute arbitrary OS commands.
suggestedAction: Pass command arguments as a list without shell invocation, or use higher-level Python APIs.

title: Debug Mode Must Not Be Enabled in Production Configuration
description: Enabling framework debug modes (e.g. app.run(debug=True) or DEBUG=True) exposes interactive debuggers and sensitive stack traces.
riskExplanation: Interactive debuggers can allow remote code execution or reveal sensitive internal environment variables.
suggestedAction: Ensure debug mode is disabled by default and configured dynamically via environment variables.

title: Insecure Object Deserialization Must Be Avoided
description: Deserializing untrusted data with pickle or unsafe PyYAML loaders can trigger arbitrary code execution.
riskExplanation: Pickle streams can execute arbitrary Python payloads during unpickling prior to application inspection.
suggestedAction: Use safe data exchange formats such as JSON or safe PyYAML parsers (yaml.safe_load).

title: Outbound HTTP Requests Must Be Validated (SSRF)
description: Executing HTTP requests to user-supplied URLs without validation allows Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).
riskExplanation: Attackers can manipulate outbound requests to access internal cloud metadata services (e.g. 169.254.169.254) or private microservices.
suggestedAction: Validate and whitelist target domain names before issuing outbound network calls.

title: File Paths Must Be Canonicalized to Prevent Path Traversal
description: Concatenating user input into file paths allows attackers to access files outside intended directories.
riskExplanation: Directory traversal sequences (e.g. '../../etc/passwd') allow unauthorized reading or writing of system files.
suggestedAction: Canonicalize target paths using pathlib.Path and verify the target remains inside the base directory.
